generated.title: Why Does Vanuatu Keep Shaking? Another M6.0 Strikes! #shorts
generated.description:
Another magnitude 6.0 earthquake struck near Vanuatu on October 28, 2026 at 02:21 UTC, about 214 km northwest of Port-Olry, according to the U.S. Geological Survey (USGS). It is the fifth earthquake of magnitude 6 or larger that USGS lists within 100 km of the October 24 epicenter since October 19.

The sequence, from the USGS catalog:
- Oct 19: M6.0 (us6000u3bc)
- Oct 20: M6.3 (us6000u3jl)
- Oct 24: M6.9 (us6000u4j2)
- Oct 24: M6.3, about 4.5 minutes later (us6000u4jb, a body-wave mb magnitude that may be revised)
- Oct 28: M6.0 (us7000ttlm)

Vanuatu sits where the Australian plate dives beneath the Pacific plate at the New Hebrides Trench. That collision loads faults with stress until they slip, and the same subduction built the volcanic island chain.

For the October 28 earthquake, USGS lists a green PAGER alert (a modeled estimate of potential impact, not a report of what happened), no tsunami flag, and one felt report. The epicenter is offshore. In the information we reviewed, no damage or casualties have been confirmed; this may change as more information becomes available. Magnitudes are USGS values and may be revised; other agencies can publish different preliminary values.

Official event page: https://earthquake.usgs.gov/earthquakes/eventpage/us7000ttlm

This video contains altered or synthetic content. The opening image is an AI-generated illustration of a Vanuatu-style coastline (GPT Image 2.5 Sunburst via ElevenLabs). It is not a photograph or footage of the earthquakes, of Port-Olry or of any affected area.
